html:
Mbanza Kongo is a town on a hilltop in northern Angola, and was the capital of the Kingdom of Kongo for centuries. Its name means "city of Kongo"; the Portuguese called it São Salvador.

The kings, the manikongo, ruled from it from about the 1300s or 1400s. When the Portuguese arrived in the 1480s it was a large town of thatched houses around the royal enclosure. In 1491 the king was baptised, and his son Afonso I made Christianity the religion of the court. Stone churches went up, among them a cathedral of 1549 whose ruins still stand, one of the oldest church buildings in sub-Saharan Africa. Kongo sent envoys to Portugal and Rome, and the town grew rich as a hub of trade, including the slave trade.

After the Portuguese of Angola killed the king at the battle of Mbwila in 1665, the kingdom broke into civil war, and by the 1670s the capital stood empty. The prophet Kimpa Vita called on people to resettle it, and King Pedro IV took it back in 1709.

It later became part of Portuguese Angola and took back its old name after independence in 1975. In 2017 it was named a World Heritage Site.
sum: Mbanza Kongo is a town on a hilltop in northern Angola, and was the capital of the Kingdom of Kongo for centuries. Its name means "city of Kongo"; the Portuguese called it São Salvador.
